mission: Lyptus Research is a small not-for-profit AI safety group in Australia. It measures how fast dangerous AI capabilities (currently offensive cyber and biosecurity) are advancing, and studies how AI systems shape each other's values as models increasingly train their successors.

key_work.title: Offensive Cybersecurity Time Horizons
key_work.plain_summary: Applied METR's time-horizon method to hacking tasks with 10 professional security experts as baselines; offensive cyber ability was doubling roughly every 6–10 months.

key_work.title: Early Experiments in Model Preferences Under Automated AI R&D
key_work.plain_summary: When AI supervisors train student models, the student's character ends up depending heavily on the supervisor.

status_note: housed within Good Ancestors Policy, a registered Australian charity
status_raw: active — housed within Good Ancestors Policy, a registered Australian charity

warnings.text: Frontier AI capabilities, including offensive cyber, are advancing rapidly.
Current evaluation methods are being saturated by the newest models.
As frontier models drive the training of their successors, they may imprint their own values.

recommendations.text: Measure dangerous capabilities against real human expert baselines.
Build independent AI safety research capacity outside the US and UK, for example in Australia.
